strengths: Novel conceptual contribution: Using adversarial learning to match intermediate marginal distributions in interpolant learning is genuinely innovative and well-motivated, clearly distinguished from pointwise matching in prior work
Solid theoretical foundations with rigorous uniqueness theorems (2.1 and 2.2) providing principled justification for regularizer design
Compelling results on targeted problems: Clear demonstration of advantages on synthetic knot data (1,200 time steps) and cell tracking where geometric variation over time is significant
Novel application domain: First application of flow matching to spatial transcriptomics coordinate inference with ~10% improvement over baselines
Strong handling of challenging settings: Demonstrates scalability to hundreds of marginal distributions and robustness to noisy, subsampled data where competing methods fail
Comprehensive experimental validation: Four diverse experiments with multiple baselines, visual comparisons, and quantitative metrics with extensive implementation details in appendix
Clear and well-structured presentation effectively motivating the problem and explaining limitations of prior approaches
weaknesses: Underperformance on standard trajectory inference benchmarks undermines practical impact: scRNA-seq experiments show 14-15% worse performance than OT-MFM on Tables 1-2, raising questions about method applicability to the primary domain

Loose theoretical-practical connection: Uniqueness theorems guarantee minimizers of regularized problems but don't address convergence of alternating GAN optimization; constraint satisfaction is only approximate with no quantified approximation error analysis

GAN training stability and reproducibility concerns: Different regularizers/hyperparameters used across experiments without systematic justification; critical details (Gaussian noise on time inputs) buried in appendix; no ablation on regularization weight λ
Limited spatial transcriptomics validation: Only one dataset tested with heavy manual preprocessing (H&E alignment); cannot assess generalization across platforms, tissues, or cancer types

Insufficient ablation studies: No direct comparison of three regularizers on same data; no sensitivity analysis for λ or coupling choice; missing analysis of whether full adversarial training is necessary
Unexplained performance trade-off: Authors acknowledge adversarial training makes scRNA-seq performance worse than OT-MFM but provide no principled solution or guidance on method selection
Missing computational cost analysis: No comparison of computational overhead from training three networks (generator, discriminator, flow matching) versus single-network baselines

strengths: Novel combination of adversarial training and flow matching for learning smooth interpolants in distribution rather than pointwise
Theoretical contributions with uniqueness theorems (2.1, 2.2) providing mathematical grounding
Impressive scalability demonstrated on 1,200 marginal distributions with sparse sampling
Strong experimental results on spatial transcriptomics tumor coordinate inference (Table 3: 98.91±2.03 vs 109.76 for OT-CFM)
Comprehensive experiments across diverse applications (synthetic knot, cell tracking, scRNA-seq, spatial transcriptomics)
Clear visual evidence of smoother learned interpolants compared to piecewise linear/cubic spline methods (Figure 8)
Well-structured methodology with clear algorithm descriptions (Algorithms 1-2)
Robustness to noisy data demonstrated in cell tracking experiments
weaknesses: Inconsistent performance on standard benchmarks: achieves 'on par' results with OT-MFM on single-cell trajectory inference (Tables 1-2), undermining claims of general superiority; improvements not statistically significant in some cases
GAN training stability and convergence not systematically analyzed; no comparison of training curves; high sensitivity to hyperparameters observed in ablations (Tables 4-6)
Gap between theory (assumes optimal discriminator, absolute continuity conditions) and practice (finite adversarial training, conditions never verified); no quantification of approximation error
Cell tracking evaluation is purely qualitative (acknowledged: 'results in mentioned figures are conclusive'); quantitative metrics available but not used
Spatial transcriptomics validated on single dataset only; limited generalization claims; no multiple ST datasets
Computational costs not compared; no wall-clock time analysis; added complexity (GAN + CFM two-stage training) vs. simpler baselines unjustified
Regularizer selection unclear for practitioners; three proposed regularizers used differently across experiments (linear for knot, piecewise-linear for ST, second-derivative for scRNA)
Limited baseline comparison fairness: dismissal of MFM time-dependent variants conflates algorithm with tuning; OT-MFM with time-independent LAND sometimes performs reasonably
Incomplete statistical testing; error bars overlap in several comparisons despite claimed improvements
Reproducibility concerns: no mention of code availability, manual spatial alignment introduces subjectivity, extensive hyperparameter tuning not fully documented
